Q5192077.label: 1940 Cuban general election
Q5192077.summary: General elections were held in Cuba on 14 July 1940. Fulgencio Batista won the presidential election running under the People's Socialist Coalition banner. Although the Partido Auténtico emerged as the largest single party in the House of Representatives, Bastista's electoral alliance, the Democratic Socialist Coalition, won a majority of seats. Voter turnout was 73%.

Q887693.label: Fidel Sánchez Hernández
Q887693.summary: Fidel Sánchez Hernández was a Salvadoran military officer, military attaché, and politician who served as President of El Salvador from 1967 to 1972 as a member of the National Conciliation Party.

Q7129997.label: 1978 Panamanian parliamentary election
Q7129997.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Panama on 6 August 1978, electing a new National Assembly of Community Representatives.

Q27957645.label: Shetland referendum, 1978
Q27957645.summary: In March 1978 a referendum was held in Shetland regarding the position of the isles within a potential Scottish Assembly. The isles' MP Jo Grimond had submitted an amendment to the Scotland Bill seeking to establish a commission in the event of a successful vote for a Scottish Assembly. This amendment faced opposition from the Secretary of State for Scotland, Bruce Millan.

Q6517645.label: Legality of the enactment of the Constitution of Ireland
Q6517645.desc: plebiscite approving the Constitution of Ireland
Q6517645.wiki: Adoption of the Constitution of Ireland
Q6517645.img: Fine Gael "Say No" Poster used in the Irish constitutional referendum of 1937.jpg
Q6517645.summary: The current Constitution of Ireland came into effect on 29 December 1937, repealing and replacing the Constitution of the Irish Free State, having been approved in a national plebiscite on 1 July 1937 with the support of 56.5% of voters in the then Irish Free State. The Constitution was closely associated with Éamon de Valera, the President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State at the time of its approval.

mentions.c: Ireland: Adoption of the Constitution of Ireland

Q2709901.label: 1969 Irish general election
Q2709901.summary: The 1969 Irish general election to the 19th Dáil was held on Wednesday, 18 June, following the dissolution of the 18th Dáil on 22 May by President Éamon de Valera on the request of Taoiseach Jack Lynch. The general election took place in 42 Dáil constituencies throughout Ireland for 144 seats in Dáil Éireann, the house of representatives of the Oireachtas, with boundary changes under the Electoral (Amendment) Act 1969. The governing Fianna Fáil won its fourth successive election.

Q2800525.label: 1948 Dutch general election
Q2800525.desc: election of the members of the House of Representatives
Q2800525.summary: General elections were held in the Netherlands on 7 July 1948. The Catholic People's Party remained the largest party in the House of Representatives, winning 32 of the 100 seats.

Q1725837.label: People's Union
Q1725837.desc: former Belgian political party in Flanders
Q1725837.summary: People's Union was a Flemish nationalist political party in Belgium, formed in 1954 as a successor to the Christian Flemish People's Union.

Q1285005.label: 1997 Croatian presidential election
Q1285005.summary: Presidential elections were held in Croatia on 15 June 1997. They were the second presidential elections held since independence in 1991. The result was a victory for incumbent president Franjo Tuđman, the leader of the Croatian Democratic Union party (HDZ), who received 61.40% of the vote and was re-elected to a second five-year term.

Q762765.label: 1948 Finnish parliamentary election
Q762765.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Finland on 1 and 2 July 1948.

Q7307661.label: Refugee controversy in Sjöbo
Q7307661.desc: September 1988 referendum in Sjöbo municipality in southern Sweden
Q7307661.summary: The refugee controversy in Sjöbo, Sweden are the surrounding events of the 1988 referendum that banned Sjöbo Municipality from admitting foreign refugees.

Q3777421.label: 1975 Danish general election
Q3777421.summary: General elections were held in Denmark on 9 January 1975. The result was a victory for the Social Democratic Party, who won 53 of the 179 seats. Voter turnout was 88% in Denmark proper, 56% in the Faroe Islands and 69% in Greenland.

Q21201293.label: 2015 Hindu Kush earthquake
Q21201293.summary: The October 2015 Hindu Kush earthquake was a magnitude 7.5 earthquake that struck South Asia on 26 October 2015, at 13:39 AFT with the epicenter 45 km north of Kuran wa Munjan, Afghanistan, at a depth of 231.0 km.

Q111968653.label: killing of Shireen Abu Akleh
Q111968653.desc: assassination of Palestinian-American journalist Shireen Abu Akleh by the Israeli forces
Q111968653.summary: On 11 May 2022, Palestinian-American journalist Shireen Abu Akleh was shot and killed by Israel Defense Forces while covering a raid at the Jenin refugee camp. Witnesses, along with the Qatari media network Al Jazeera, for which Abu Akleh had worked for 25 years, reported that an Israeli soldier shot her in the head.

mentions.c: Palestine: Assassination: killing of Shireen Abu Akleh

Q36749.label: Beer Hall Putsch
Q36749.desc: attempted coup d'état in Weimar Republic
Q36749.summary: The Beer Hall Putsch, also known as the Munich Putsch, was a failed coup d'état led by Nazi Party leader Adolf Hitler, General Erich Ludendorff, and other Kampfbund leaders in Munich, Bavaria, on 8–9 November 1923, during the Weimar Republic. Inspired by Benito Mussolini's March on Rome, Hitler's goal was to use Munich as a base for a march against Germany's national government in Berlin.

Q19606413.label: anti-Western sentiment
Q19606413.img: Protests after US decision to withdraw from JCPOA, around former US embassy, Tehran - 8 May 2018 26.jpg
Q19606413.summary: Anti-Western sentiment, also known as anti-Atlanticism, Westophobia or Westernophobia, refers to the broad opposition or hostility towards the people, culture, or policies of the Western world.

Q181133.label: Trotskyism
Q181133.desc: variety of Marxism developed by Leon Trotsky
Q181133.summary: Trotskyism is the political ideology and branch of Marxism and Leninism developed by Russian revolutionary and intellectual Leon Trotsky along with some other members of the Left Opposition and the Fourth International. Trotsky described himself as an orthodox Marxist, a revolutionary Marxist, and a Bolshevik–Leninist as well as a follower of Karl Marx, Friedrich Engels, Vladimir Lenin, Karl Liebknecht, and Rosa Luxemburg. His relationship with Lenin has been a source of intense historical debate.
